content.text:
The environment captures screenshots automatically at desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844. So the game should look good immediately on load (auto-start likely clicking a start button). Need to handle canvas rendering, no external deps needed (plain HTML/JS canvas 2D is safest — no network deps).

Design the game: "The world remembers everything you do." Open-world survival with adaptive NPCs and enemies that learn your strategies.

Given constraints (web, screenshot capture, mobile), a 2D top-down canvas game is ideal. But "open world survival" with memory needs to be *visible* in the first screenshot to be compelling. I'll make a gorgeous top-down survival world with:

- Procedural world: biomes, trees, rocks, water, camp, ruins.
- Player: survival stats (health, hunger, warmth, stamina), day/night cycle, weather.
- Base building? Crafting? Keep depth but manageable.
- Core hook: **The Chronicle** — a memory system recording every action (kills, tactics used, places visited, kindness/cruelty, times fled). NPCs reference memories in dialogue. Enemies spawn with adaptations based on your tactics (e.g., if you use ranged attacks, they carry shields/bum rush; if you sneak, they get torches/dogs; if you trap, they avoid traps). World changes: burned forest stays burned, killed wolf packs cause deer overpopulation, etc.
- Factions/villages remembering reputation.

Deliver a polished single-page game with:
1. Title screen overlay ("The Hollow") with start.
2. Canvas world, smooth camera, minimap.
3. HUD: survival bars, day counter, memory/adaptation panel.
4. NPC dialogue with memory lines.
5. Combat: melee swing, ranged bow, sneak, traps. Enemies learn.
6. Chronicle panel (press M) showing recorded memories and adaptations.
7. Mobile touch joystick + buttons.

That's ambitious. Let's scope to a tight, high-quality implementation, maybe ~2000-2500 lines split into modules: no build step, ES modules with plain index.html. Files: index.html, css/style.css, js/*.js. Static server serves files, so modules work.

Plan architecture:
- `index.html` — canvas, HUD overlays, title screen, panels.
- `styles.css`
- `js/main.js` — bootstrap, loop, input.
- `js/world.js` — procedural generation (regions, props, villages).
- `js/memory.js` — Chronicle: events, tags, adaptation rules.
- `js/entities.js` — player, NPCs, wildlife, enemies, projectiles.
- `js/ui.js` — HUD, dialogue, chronicle, minimap.
- `js/audio.js` — optional WebAudio simple synth (no assets).
- `js/render.js` — draw functions.

Keep the art style striking: muted earth palette, fog of war, long shadows, stylized. Since screenshot is a static frame, visuals must read instantly: a top-down map with cozy village, firelight, trees, HUD with "THE WORLD REMEMBERS" ticker. Title screen maybe better for first impression but capture auto-start may click a start button — capture-start tries clicking selector. Default CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR empty; it looks for common start buttons? Let me check capture-start.mjs to know if auto-start clicks.

Auto-start will click exactly one visible button labeled "Start", "Play", etc. So the title screen should have exactly one such button, label "Begin" would not auto-click (regex start|play). Make the button "Play" or "Start". It must be unique. Good: title screen with one "Begin Survival"? regex requires exactly "start", "play", "start game", "start now", "play game", "play now". Use "Play" — auto-clicked. Then screenshot 1s later shows game. Must ensure game visuals ready immediately at start (world pre-generated).

Architecture plan. Let's think about the game design in detail so it's genuinely fun and showcases memory.

**Title: "THE HOLLOW REMEMBERS"** maybe "REMEMBRANCE" or "ASHFALL". Let's pick **"The World Remembers"** as subtitle. Name: **"HOLLOWMOOR"**. Hmm. Concept: survival in a valley where the land keeps a ledger. Title: **"THE LEDGER"**? I like **"ASHFALL: The World Remembers"**. Simpler: **"H O L L O W"**.

Game name: **"Hollowmoor"** — a fog-drowned valley. Subtitle "the valley forgets nothing."

**Core loop (15-20 min session):**
- Top-down open world (~4000x3000) with biomes: meadow, pine forest, ash bog, ruins, village.
- Player has health, hunger, warmth, stamina. Day/night cycle (~4 min/day). Night = enemies.
- Resources: wood, stone, fiber, berries, meat. Craft campfire, spear, bow, snare trap.
- NPCs: village of Hollowmoor, 5 named NPCs with dialogue generated from memory. Reputation per faction/village. They comment on your actions: "You burned the north wood. The children still cough."
- Enemies: "The Hollowed" — night creatures that adapt. Also rival scavengers.
- Memory: every significant action recorded as an event with tags. Adaptation engine computes profile: aggression, stealth, ranged, trap usage, mercy, arson, theft. Enemies get traits accordingly: e.g. "They keep their distance now — shields raised against arrows." Wolves learn to flank. Village gates close at night if you're distrusted. Traps become avoided.
- Journal "THE LEDGER" (Tab/M) lists memories in-world prose + "WHAT THEY LEARNED" adaptations with icons.
- Death resets day but remembers (roguelite?) — maybe keep simple: death → "The valley remembers you. It always will." respawn at camp with memory intact and new adaptation. Nice hook, cheap to implement.
- Win condition: survive 5 nights? Or build a beacon? Add objective: light three signal fires at ancient cairns to escape the valley. That gives direction and an end screen. Good.

**Controls:** WASD/arrows, mouse aim + click attack, E interact, Space dodge/roll? Shift sprint, Q place trap, 1/2/3 tools, Tab ledger. Mobile: joystick left, buttons right (attack, interact, dodge), tap panel buttons.

**Visuals:** Hand-drawn-ish canvas 2D. Top-down with subtle pseudo-3D (trees drawn as canopy with offset trunk shadow). Palette: deep teal-green night, amber firelight. Fog vignette. Particles for fire/rain. Day/night tinted overlay with radial light around campfires/player. Long shadows via ellipses. Water animated.

Show "memory" visually: the ground near places where you did things has "echo" markers? Maybe memory motes floating at event locations. Nice: small glowing sigils at event sites; hover reveals "Here, you ...". Adds visible memory.

**Performance:** draw only visible props; generate ~1200 props. Fine.

**Screenshot quality:** Title screen with animated backdrop? Title screen would be captured only if auto-start fails. It auto-clicks Play. Then game screen at 1s after. Show a brief intro "Day 1 — Dawn" cinematic overlay? Could obscure. Better: game starts with camera on village at dawn, HUD visible, and a "ledger" toast: "The valley is watching." A first-run tutorial card maybe. Screenshot should be rich: village huts with smoke, campfire, NPCs, trees, HUD bars, objective, minimap, memory ticker. Good.

Let me avoid overlay modal at start. Auto-click Play → immediate game.

Implementation details:

World generation with seeded RNG (mulberry32). Define world size 3600x2600. Regions via noise-ish: use value noise from seeded grid for biome; simpler: distance-based meadow center + patches. I'll implement simple 2D value noise (hash-based, smooth interpolation, few octaves) for elevation/moisture. Biome from elevation/moisture thresholds: water, bog, forest, meadow, ashland, rock. Village at center-ish with flattened area. Landmarks: 3 cairns at edges, ruins, hunter camp, lake.

Props: trees (pine/oak/dead), rocks, bushes, reeds, flowers, mushrooms, stumps, bones, ruins pillars. Collision for trees/rocks (circle colliders) maybe limited; simpler: player collides with solid props using spatial grid for perf. Let's include collision to feel real, using per-cell lists and circle resolution.

Entities:
- Player: pos, vel, angle, radius, stats, inventory, tools, attack cooldowns, animation state, sneak/sprint, dodge.
- NPCs: 5 villagers with names, roles, wander behavior, dialogue triggers, memory-conditioned lines; can follow/hide at night. Interact E shows dialogue panel with their recollection.
- Wildlife: deer (flee), rabbits, crows; wolves at night, "Hollowed" creatures spawning from ash zones increasing nightly. Hunt deer for meat.
- Enemies: Hollowed (melee, adapt traits), Raiders? Keep one enemy family plus wolves. Adaptation traits: shielded (anti-ranged), swift (anti-flee), sniffer (anti-stealth), trapper-aware (avoid traps), pack (numbers if you're aggressive), armored (if melee heavy). Visual differences (shield, red eyes, tall, etc.) and behaviors: shield reduces ranged damage; swift faster; sniffer detection radius big; trap-avoid; encircling.
- Trap entity placed by player, triggers on enemies.
- Campfire, beacon sites.
- Projectiles (arrows), particles, floating texts, footstep marks.

Memory system:
```
memory = {
  events: [{day,time,type,label,tags,pos,weight}],
  traits: {ranged, melee, stealth, traps, fire, mercy, theft, kills, flee, exploration},
  adaptations: Set of ids,
  places: {burned: [...],}.
}
```
record(type, text, tags, pos) updates counters; after each record, evaluate adaptations thresholds -> unlock, push "world learns" toast + chronicle entry. Traits tempered: using bow increases ranged. Enemies adapt on next spawn/night.

NPC dialogue assembly from memories: each NPC has personality filter; choose top relevant memory by tags; lines templates referencing memories. E.g., "You loosed nine arrows last night. The Hollowed came back with shields." Also generic lines per role/day/weather.

Consequences visible in world: if fire trait high, burned patches appear where fire used; if you killed villagers... maybe skip villager killing. Reputation: helping (give berries, defend) raises; stealing (take from huts) lowers. Village gate lighting: lanterns count.

Objective: Light the three cairns with ember from the village hearth? Simpler: each cairn needs 3 wood + torch; interact to light; when all three lit, "The way opens" ending overlay with your chronicle summary ("Your valley": stats, adaptations, deeds). Time ~10 min. Night 5 pressure. Death→respawn, lose some resources, memory persists, "The Hollowed learned from your fall."

Daily cycle: 4 minutes real time? 180s day, 90s night maybe. Screenshot at start: dawn. Start time day 1 07:00. Day length 240s full cycle. Night starts 19:00.

Weather: rain occasionally, fog at night. Particles.

Audio: WebAudio synthesized wind, fire crackle, hits, UI. Start after user gesture (Play click). Keep subtle; mute toggle. Adds a lot of feel for low cost. I'll implement modest synth.

HUD:
- Top-left: day/time + location name.
- Bars: health (red), stamina (amber), hunger (orange), warmth (blue). Compact.
- Bottom-left: inventory resources with icons (wood/stone/fiber/berry/meat counts).
- Bottom-center: tool slots 1-3 (Axe/Spear/Bow) + trap count.
- Top-right: minimap with memory sigils, village, cairns.
- Right side: "THE VALLEY LEARNS" ticker with 2 latest adaptations, "Ledger [Tab]" button.
- Objective top-center: "Light the cairns 0/3".
- Dialogue panel bottom when talking.
- Craft panel (C) overlay.

Mobile: first-run detection for touch; show joystick + buttons. Make HUD adaptive via CSS. Add `touch-action: none`, safe-area insets. Player aim: on mobile, attack targets nearest enemy in facing direction.

I need to be realistic about implementation size. Let's write clean modular JS, test with playwright, iterate visuals. This is a large build; I'll aim for ~2500 lines total across modules, well-structured.

Files:
- index.html
- styles.css
- js/util.js (rng, noise, math, easing)
- js/world.js (gen, props, biomes, collisions, minimap data)
- js/memory.js (chronicle + adaptation)
- js/entities.js (player, npc, animals, hollowed, traps, projectiles)
- js/game.js (state, loop, input, combat, interactions, crafting, day/night, objectives, save?)
- js/render.js (world render, entities, effects, lighting, weather)
- js/ui.js (DOM HUD, ledger, dialogue, craft, title, ending, minimap canvas)
- js/audio.js
- js/main.js

Save to localStorage so memory persists between sessions? "The world remembers" across playthroughs — cool: persist chronicle across reloads with "Cycle" count. But screenshot tests: start screen would show past memories maybe empty. Persist optional: yes, store world memory; on new game, ask "The valley remembers you (Cycle 3). Continue?" That complicates start. Keep persistence: if localStorage has memory, title button changes? Auto-capture may click. Let's persist but title always "Play" and start with memory carried ("The valley remembers. Cycle N."). This is a strong hook. But adaptation from last session may confuse; fine, that's the point. For fresh screenshot, localStorage empty in new browser each capture — good.

Ending: reaching 3 cairns → overlay with "THE WAY OPENS" and chronicle summary, button "Begin Again" (a new cycle where world remembers — carries memory). On death: respawn overlay "The valley remembers your fall" — continue button? For screenshot, avoid modals. Deaths rare in first seconds.

Now, gameplay specifics:

Player movement: speed 150 px/s; sprint 230 with stamina drain. Sneak 80 (Shift? no shift is sprint). Ctrl sneak. Dodge Space with stamina.

Camera zoom ~1.0 at 1440x900 showing ~1440x900 world px. World 3600x2600. Character radius 12, drawn ~26 px. Trees 40-80 px. Fine.

Combat:
- Melee: LMB / J. Arc swing radius 46, damage 22 (+tool), cooldown 0.45s. Stamina 8.
- Bow: requires arrows (craft 5 arrows from wood+fiber). Hold right? Use tool switch 2 = bow, LMB fires arrow, damage 26, cooldown 0.7s.
- Spear: longer reach, damage 30, cooldown 0.8.
- Axe: chops trees (hold attack near tree) + melee 18.
- Tool selection 1/2/3; mobile cycle button.
- Traps: Q place snare (1 fiber +1 wood? inventory simplification: craft from fiber), enemies trigger → immobilized + damage.

Resources: chop tree with axe near → wood x3 over 3 hits? Simpler: hold attack near tree with axe, tree gets hit points, falls, wood +4; tree persists as stump (world memory: "you cleared the north grove" and forest thinning visual!). That's a nice world-state change: trees you cut stay cut. But enemies adapt? no. Fine, but regrow at new cycle.

Mining rocks for stone, bushes for berries, reeds for fiber, hunt deer for meat, cook meat at fire (eat raw = risk? skip).

Survival: hunger drains slowly, warmth drains at night unless near fire; health regen when hunger > 50 and warmth > 30. Eating berries +12 hunger, cooked meat +35, raw meat +20 with health -5. Campfire craft at spot: wood 5 + stone 3; provides light/warmth, cook.

Village: huts, NPCs, central hearth (permanent fire), storage crate? Interactions: talk, give berries (+rep), rest (skip to dawn, costs hunger), take supplies (steal, -rep, memory tag theft).

NPC memory dialogue: use `dialogueFor(npc)` generating 2-3 sentences combining memory lines + role line. Display name, portrait circle, text; E/space continue. Keep a deterministic pick.

Enemy AI:
- Hollowed spawn at night from ash patches/cairn areas, count scales with night+aggression memory.
- States: idle/patrol → chase if detection (radius modified by stealth/sniff) → attack (melee windup) → stagger/flee at low hp.
- Adaptation traits applied to spawned enemies based on chronicle profile:
  - `shielded`: 40% ranged resist, visual shield.
  - `swift`: +18% speed (if you flee a lot).
  - `keen`: detection +60% (if stealth).
  - `warded`: avoid traps, +trap resist (if traps).
  - `pack`: spawn +1 each (if aggressive/kills).
  - `emberhide`: resist fire/less fear of campfire (if fire use) — enemies can enter firelight.
  - `flanker`: circle-strafe (if ranged).
- Each adaptation has codex entry text and ledger card.
- Show enemy trait glyphs above health bar, so screenshot can show "SHIELDED" etc. On first night maybe one appears. To ensure screenshot shows adaptation... it won't in 1s. But ledger panel can be opened by us in verification screenshot. Fine.

Night pressure and objective: cairns at three far locations, lighting requires 1 torch each (craft torch: wood1+fiber1) and interaction with fire? Keep: carry "ember" from hearth? Simpler: light cairn needs 3 wood + torch; auto-consume. Cairns emit light column visible on minimap. Each cairn lighting triggers a "The valley stirs" wave. Final: ending overlay.

Distance: cairns ~1000-1400 px from village → travel 10-20s each way, encounters en route. Session 8-12 min. Day length 240s is enough for 2-3 days.

Time: start Day 1, 08:00. Night at 19:00 (real ~110s at 1 game-minute per 0.5s? Let's compute: full day 24h game = 240s → 1h = 10s. 08:00→19:00 = 110s. Good. Dawn at 06:00.

Map / fog: draw distant terrain with slight desaturation; vision radius limited at night by radial gradient darkness. Day full visibility.

Rendering style detail:
- Ground: base color per biome with noise speckles cached on offscreen canvas? Generate a big offscreen terrain canvas (3600x2600) at 1px per 2? That's 9.3M px — fine as one canvas (memory ~37MB) maybe heavy on mobile. Instead render ground via layered tiles: create pattern canvases per biome (256x256) and draw with clip? Simpler: draw visible ground cells as rects from a coarse biome grid (e.g., 40px cells) with color variation and dithering; plus scattered detail props. 1440x900 / 40 = 36x23 cells = ~830 rects/frame — fine, and gives nice tile texture with slight per-cell color jitter. Use 32px cells maybe 1300 rects. OK. Add parallax noise patches (drawn blobs) cached? Keep cell colors with smooth-ish look: each cell drawn as rect with color from biome + noise; seams visible. Better: draw blobs: pre-generate 2000 soft "patches" (ellipses) across world with biome colors and alpha; draw visible ones. Plus base fill gradient. That gives painterly look. Combine: base per-biome large fill via coarse cells with rounded large ellipses (radius 60-120, alpha 0.25) for blend. Props on top.

Palette:

Particles: fire embers, smoke, rain, snow?, dust on move, blood sparingly, sparkle on memory sigils. Ambient floating motes (like spores) for mood.

Colors: bone #e8e0cf, ink #12161a, ember #e0763c, moss #8fa06a. Panels with translucent dark, thin border, blur. Title screen with big serif title, rule lines, animated canvas world behind (live world running slowly?)
```js
export class Noise {
  constructor(seed=1){ this.seed=seed|0; }
  hash(ix, iy) {
    let h = Math.imul(ix, 374761393) + Math.imul(iy, 668265263) + Math.imul(this.seed, 1442695041);
    h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 1274126177);
    return ((h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0) / 4294967295;
  }
  value(x,y){
    const x0=Math.floor(x), y0=Math.floor(y);
    const fx=x-x0, fy=y-y0;
    const ux=fx*fx*(3-2*fx), uy=fy*fy*(3-2*fy);
    const a=this.hash(x0,y0), b=this.hash(x0+1,y0), c=this.hash(x0,y0+1), d=this.hash(x0+1,y0+1);
    return lerp(lerp(a,b,ux), lerp(c,d,ux), uy);
  }
  fbm(x,y,oct=4,lac=2,gain=0.5){
    let amp=0.5, freq=1, sum=0, norm=0;
    for(let i=0;i<oct;i++){ sum += amp*this.value(x*freq, y*freq); norm+=amp; amp*=gain; freq*=lac; }
    return sum/norm;
  }
}
```

```
  // ash near cairns

  // rock

  return 'meadow';
}
```

## Objective
- Build a playable open-world survival web game in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` from the pitch: “An open-world survival game where the world remembers everything you do. NPCs adapt, enemies learn your strategies, and no two playthroughs are the same.”

## Requirements
- Static browser game served from `index.html` (no build step/framework); must work on desktop and mobile (touch controls, safe areas, 390×844).
- Must visually demonstrate the memory/adaptation hook, not just claim it.
- One visible button labeled exactly `Play` on the title screen so screenshot auto-start clicks it.
- Audio must be gesture-initiated and asset-free.

## Decisions
- Game named **HOLLOWMOOR**; top-down 2D canvas survival with day/night cycle, village NPCs, Hollowed enemies, gathering/crafting, three cairns as win condition.
- Built-in **The Ledger** chronicle: records deeds/traits, unlocks seven enemy adaptations (`shielded`, `swift`, `keen`, `warded`, `pack`, `emberhide`, `marrowbow`) with visible behavioral and visual changes; persists via `localStorage` key `hollowmoor.chronicle.v2`, carrying into new cycles.
- Procedural seeded world (3800×2800), biomes, paths, village huts, ruins, three cairns; trees chopped/stumps persist within a run.
- NPC dialogue generated from traits/adaptations/reputation; sharing berries raises mercy/reputation.
- Death is a memory event with respawn at hearth; ending overlay after lighting all cairns, then “Walk in again” starts a new cycle retaining lessons.
- Implemented as ES modules split by responsibility: config, util, world, memory, audio, game, combat, draw, render, ui, main.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css` with full HUD/title/ledger/craft/dialogue/death/ending/touch markup and responsive dark-ember visual design.
- `js/util.js` (RNG/noise/color/math), `js/world.js` (generation, props, colliders, paths, minimap/ground canvases), `js/memory.js` (Chronicle + adaptations), `js/audio.js` (synth soundscape), `js/config.js` (tools/recipes/NPC definitions).
- `js/game.js` core loop, player movement/survival, time/weather, NPCs/dialogue, animals, fires, interactions, crafting, ledger/panels, death/respawn/new cycle.
- `js/combat.js` player attack/dodge/ember/traps, enemy spawn/AI, projectiles, adaptation-driven stats.
- `js/draw.js` hand-drawn prop/village/cairn/character/animal/echo rendering.
- `js/render.js` world rendering, lighting, weather, vignette, minimap.
- `js/ui.js` DOM wiring: HUD, resources, hotbar, toasts, learnings, ledger, craft, dialogue, touch joystick/buttons, sound toggle.

### Active
- `js/main.js` not yet created (bootstrap, canvas/DPR resize, RAF loop, session start).
- No runtime verification yet; code has not been syntax-checked or loaded in a browser.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js`: instantiate `Sound`, `Game(canvas, sound)`, `UI(game)`, resize handler calling `game.setViewport(w, h, dpr)`, RAF loop calling `game.update(dt)` and `render(ctx, game)`, DPR cap 2.
2. Start dev server per repo `start.sh`/runtime scripts and syntax-check modules (e.g. `node --check`).
3. Run Playwright screenshot verification (desktop 1440×900, mobile 390×844), confirm title auto-start, no console/page errors, gameplay visible within 1s.
4. Inspect screenshots, fix visual/JS issues, then test interactions: movement, attack, gather, craft, ledger (Tab), cairn lighting, adaptation unlock, death/respawn.
5. Clean known bugs: dead code in `world.js` prop-generation loop (`for (const c of cairns) { biome === 'ash' && null; }`); verify `updateNpcs` exit-hut positioning; confirm `draw.js` uses `roundRect` supported.
6. Add CSS touch-mode rules if needed (`body.touch-mode .hotbar { display:none }`, hide desktop hints).

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: UI skeleton, IDs used by `ui.js`, sole `Play` button.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all HUD/title/panel/touch styling and responsive rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: central state/update loop; imports `combat.js`; contains `// __PART2__` replacement already completed.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/combat.js`: enemy adaptations and combat; exports `enemyCap`, `spawnEnemy`, `spawnWave`, `updateEnemies`, `updateProjectiles`, `updateTraps`, `damageEnemy`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/render.js`: `render(ctx, game)` and `drawMinimap(canvas, game)`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/ui.js`: DOM wiring, touch input, HUD/panels; expects `game` methods/properties.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/draw.js`: all canvas art primitives; uses `ctx.roundRect`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: procedural world, collisions, ground/minimap canvases.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/memory.js`: Chronicle persistence and `ADAPTATIONS` definitions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/config.js`: tools, recipes, NPC data, `TIME_SCALE`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesized audio (`init`, `sfx`, `setNight`, `setMuted`).
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/util.js`: seeded RNG/noise/color helpers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: launches default static server via `RUNTIME_DIR` script.

## Important Context
- `Game` constructor is `new Game(canvas, sound)` and sets `game.ui` later when `new UI(game)` is constructed.
- Capture harness auto-clicks a visible button whose text matches `start|play`; keep exactly one such visible button on title screen.
- `UI` calls `game.audio.init()` on Play, then `game.start()`, which records the arrival event and shows HUD.
- `render.js` maintains module-level `lightCanvas`, `grainPattern`, `vignetteCache`; requires browser DOM (canvas creation).
- `game.setViewport(w, h, dpr)` sets zoom (`clamp(min(w,h)/860, 0.72, 1.06)`); must be called initially and on resize.
- Browser must serve ES modules over HTTP; use repo start flow (`start.sh`/`RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs`), expected port 3002 per environment notes.
- The game references `game.currentInteract`, `game.emberRing`, `game.player.hitT`, `game.chronicle.fresh`; these are set in existing modules.
- Known suspicious code to review: `world.js` cairn skip loop dead statement; `ui.js` `updateHud` traverses `bar.parentElement.parentElement` expecting `.vital`; `game.craft('cook')` cost deduction intentionally leaves meat at `-1` once (verify).
- Changes are uncommitted; no git commit/push performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable open-world survival web game in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround` from the pitch: “An open-world survival game where the world remembers everything you do. NPCs adapt, enemies learn your strategies, and no two playthroughs are the same.”

## Requirements
- Static browser game served from `index.html` (no build step/framework); must work on desktop and mobile (touch controls, safe areas, 390×844).
- Must visually demonstrate the memory/adaptation hook, not just claim it.
- One visible button labeled exactly `Play` on the title screen so screenshot auto-start clicks it.
- Audio must be gesture-initiated and asset-free.

## Decisions
- Game named **HOLLOWMOOR**; top-down 2D canvas survival with day/night cycle, village NPCs, Hollowed enemies, gathering/crafting, three cairns as win condition.
- Built-in **The Ledger** chronicle records deeds/traits, unlocks seven enemy adaptations (`shielded`, `swift`, `keen`, `warded`, `pack`, `emberhide`, `marrowbow`) with visible behavioral and visual changes; persists via `localStorage` key `hollowmoor.chronicle.v2`, carrying into new cycles.
- Procedural seeded world (3800×2800), biomes, paths, village huts, ruins, three cairns; trees chopped/stumps persist within a run.
- NPC dialogue generated from traits/adaptations/reputation; sharing berries raises mercy/reputation.
- Death is a memory event with respawn at hearth; ending overlay after lighting all cairns, then “Walk in again” starts a new cycle retaining lessons.
- Implemented as ES modules split by responsibility: config, util, world, memory, audio, game, combat, draw, render, ui, main.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `styles.css`, and all `js/*.js` modules including `js/main.js` bootstrap, DPR-capped resize, RAF loop, and debug `window.hollowmoor`.
- Runtime verified through Playwright on desktop 1440×900 and mobile 390×844: title auto-start, movement, combat, gathering, crafting, ledger, NPC dialogue, cairn lighting, death/respawn, ending/new cycle, persistence, touch joystick/buttons.
- Fixed startup crash from `const sp` reassignment in `Game.addParticles`; removed dead cairn loop in `world.js`; fixed `dist` import in `draw.js`.
- Fixed crafting being blocked from the craft panel (`craft()` now allows mode `'craft'`).
- Fixed mobile title overflow by reducing mobile `h1` to `clamp(40px, 12.2vw, 72px)`; added touch-specific title hint.
- Added touch-specific close labels (`×`, removed `E`/`ESC`), hid prompt kbd in touch mode, made Sable’s Tab hint touch-aware.
- Moved mobile toasts below HUD to avoid covering vitals/minimap; increased mobile ghost-button height; added ending mobile padding.
- Added `roundRect` fallback for older mobile WebViews; made `record()` trigger near-immediate chronicle save.
- Verification scripts exist in `/tmp/opencode/`: `flow.mjs`, `flow2.mjs`, `stress.mjs`, `persist.mjs`, `dialogue.mjs`, `mobilepanels.mjs`, `adaptshot.mjs`, `bowprobe.mjs`, etc.
- No page errors in tested flows. Browser screenshot harness auto-start is intermittent only under parallel CPU load; sequential runs succeed.

### Active
- Final visual/gameplay polish and last verification pass.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Re-run `bash capture.sh` sequentially with `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002/ CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/opencode/shots CAPTURE_STRICT=1`; inspect final desktop/mobile screenshots after latest CSS changes.
2. Re-test mobile title, mobile panels, dialogue, and touch labels after the latest edits.
3. Consider a final gameplay balance/clarity pass (night darkness/enemy visibility, starting spawn framing).
4. Run `node --check` across modules once more, then commit all changes if requested.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: UI skeleton, IDs, sole `Play` button, touch-specific hint.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: all HUD/title/panel/touch/responsive styling; recent mobile fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/main.js`: bootstrap, `roundRect` polyfill, resize, RAF loop, debug handle.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: core state/update, crafting fix, save timing, NPC dialogue.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/combat.js`: enemy adaptations, combat, projectiles, traps.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/ui.js`: DOM wiring, touch controls, HUD/panels, touch labels.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/render.js`: world rendering, lighting, weather, minimap.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/draw.js`: canvas art primitives; uses `dist` and `roundRect`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/world.js`: procedural world/collisions/ground canvas.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/memory.js`: Chronicle persistence and adaptation definitions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/config.js`: tools, recipes, NPC definitions, `TIME_SCALE = 6`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/capture.sh`: screenshot capture entry point.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: static server entry point.
- `/tmp/opencode/`: Playwright probe and screenshot scripts, screenshots.

## Important Context
- Static server running at `http://localhost:3002/` via `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`.
- `Game` constructor is `new Game(canvas, sound)`; `new UI(game)` sets `game.ui`.
- Capture harness auto-clicks a visible button whose text matches `start|play`; keep exactly one such button visible on title.
- `game.setViewport(w,h,dpr)` must run on load/resize; zoom is `clamp(min(w,h)/860, 0.72, 1.06)`.
- Camera leads 42px toward aim, so screen center is not exactly the player; aim clicks must target on-screen enemy positions.
- `game.mode` values include `title`, `play`, `ledger`, `craft`, `dialogue`, `dead`, `ending`; `craft()` intentionally accepts `play` and `craft`.
- `localStorage` key is `hollowmoor.chronicle.v2`; persisted cycle/unlocked adaptations verified across reload.
- Changes are uncommitted; no git commit/push performed.
- Latest bow test: 3 arrows killed spawned enemy, `bow` trait 2, `kills` 1, no errors.
